system.summary: Syllabic substitution: base glyph = consonant row, superscript digit = syllable in the row (homophones), bare glyphs = single letters, a small code (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Cesar, Pontifex, Italia ...) and many nulls.

diacritics.note: superscript digits 1-9 select the syllable within a consonant row; two-digit superscripts mostly nulls or codes

system.sibling_key: The same key in R8476, R8589, R8590 (all with contemporary decipherments) and R8613; used to rebuild the key. Tomokiyo's partial table (cryptiana henryviii.htm) also used.
system.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from the former 'superscript' target: Gilino R8572 is a different (Milanese) system with its own key and now has its own folder (targets/gilino1527/).

prior_solution.where: R8476, R8589, R8590 deciphered at the time (St.P. VI 552; L&P 5282; interlinear) and in print; R8613 called 'undeciphered' in L&P iv 3291, which summarises the original Vit. B IX 127 in English; Tomokiyo's partial table.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tried DECODE (login required), BL digitised manuscripts and Gallica for images.
Fetched full-size DECODE images of R8476, R8589, R8590, R8613, R8572 with the login cookie; no DOC transcriptions on the records.

L&P iv on BHO and St.P. VI/VII on archive.org: R8476 = L&P 2727 printed with decipher in St.P. VI 552; R8589 = L&P 5282 with the Latin decipherment printed; R8590 = L&P 5300; R8613 = L&P 3291 no. 2, a duplicate of 22 July 1527 'undeciphered'.
Transcribed R8589's cipher and aligned it with the L&P 5282 Latin; the decipherer's diagonal strokes mark nulls.
Established the system: consonant-row glyph + superscript syllable digit, bare glyphs single letters, nulls, codes.
Transcribed R8613 in full (814 tokens) from line crops.
Applied the R8589/R8590 key to R8613: Lautrec, Avemaria, dilationem, perpetuam divisionem came out.
Extended the key from R8613's own context and the L&P 3291 summary (conditiones, duraturam, parcendum pro liberatione filiorum, milliones, colloquia ...).
Sub-agent transcribed R8476 (845 tokens) and aligned it with St.P. VI, giving the code words (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Pontifex, Gallia ...).
R8613 read to 780 of 814 tokens (95.8%) with the merged key; 34 tokens in a few single-occurrence stretches stay open.
Second image pass on R8613 P1 l4 and l6 at full resolution: 'p10 +?' re-read as p+ and ɔ10, 'v3' as y3.
With h = s (as in R8476), u8 = o, Q1 = i and nulls xi14, Z9, ɔ10, Z2: 'Et si pinguiores eis offerret conditiones' and 'nisi hec eos spes nutriret'; R8613 measured at 797 of 814 tokens (97.9%).

Split from the former combined target 'superscript' (Ghinucci R8613 with Gilino R8572), after George Lasry pointed out that the two letters share only superscript numbering: different writers, languages and keys (the Worcester syllabary vs the Sforza key R5258). Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 804 tokens, 200 types, la order 4: reading -2.135 per letter; random keys -3.26 (z 11.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.365 (mean -2.397, z 14.9); annealer on the real text -2.342. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R8613 transcription and reading; R8589 and R8476 token-value alignments; key.tsv, key.md, r8476_key.tsv. R8590 (key source, first cipher line read against the interlinear) has no transcription file in the folder
Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R8613 reads (A); the R8589 and R8476 files are key-building worksheets, relabelled not prose. Claim unchanged.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged.

Full-texts pass: R8590 had no outcome.texts entry. No file of its cipher exists in the folder (9 Oct: first line read against the interlinear, values only kept in key.tsv). Tried the DECODE image anonymously: the full image is refused ('Insufficient permissions to see the full image'), only a 200x287 thumbnail is served. Opened L&P iv 5300 on British History Online and saved its entry, which quotes the deciphered Latin, as r8590_lp5300.md with the ten key.tsv rows citing R8590; entry listed as 'not prose' with transcription_missing.

texts.label: R8613, Ghinucci to Wolsey, duplicate of 22 July 1527
texts.summary: Girolamo Ghinucci, Bishop of Worcester, at the Emperor's court, reports that the Imperialists want to draw Henry VIII to themselves and part him from the French king, that the French offered three millions through Avemaria, that the Imperial envoy to the Pope has no commission for his release, and the rumour that Wolsey goes to France to separate the English and French church from Rome 'ad perpetuam divisionem'. L&P iv 3291 records that this duplicate was not deciphered at the time; 17 of 814 tokens remain open.

texts.label: R8589, Ghinucci to Wolsey, Valladolid, 12 Feb 1529 (key source)
texts.summary: Sibling letter whose cipher passage is printed deciphered in L&P iv 5282 ('Cum animadvertissemus ...'); the file gives each token with its value aligned to that plaintext, and was the first key source.
texts.note: A glyph-to-letter alignment worksheet (token=value pairs, struck nulls) used to build the key; the Latin of the passage is printed in L&P iv 5282 (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R8476, Ghinucci to Wolsey, Poissy, 24 Dec 1526 (key source)
texts.summary: Sibling letter printed with its deciphered passages in State Papers Henry VIII vol. VI pp. 552-556 (from the contemporary Record Office decipher); the file aligns the 845 cipher tokens with that text and gave the code words (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Cesar, Pontifex ...).
texts.note: A glyph transcription with token=value alignments and a glyph legend, used as key source; its decipherment is printed in State Papers VI 552 (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R8590, Ghinucci to [Wolsey], Valladolid, 15 Feb 1529 (key source)
texts.transcription_missing: Only the first cipher line was read token by token against the interlinear decipherment (9 Oct 2026); its values went into key.tsv and the token line was not saved. The DECODE full image (IMG_R8590_I39633_P1.jpg) is behind the DECODE login: an anonymous request on 14 Nov 2026 returns the placeholder 'Insufficient permissions to see the full image', and the earlier copy in img/ is git-ignored and not in this checkout. A logged-in fetch of the image, then a token transcription in the glyph names of key.md, would supply it.
texts.summary: Sibling letter with an interlinear decipherment of the time on the page; L&P iv 5300 quotes its ciphered Latin ('non discederem ex Hispania quousque singula ab Urbe mihi et nuncio pontificis huc mittenda perbecta essent'). The file gives the calendar entry and the ten key.tsv rows that cite this letter as evidence.
texts.note: Key source, not a reading of ours: the calendar entry of L&P iv 5300 (the ciphered words in italics there) and the list of key values taken from the page; no token transcription of the letter is held.
